h: Alice, goats and the Great Orme
p: Llandudno has a famous literary connection. Alice Liddell, the real girl who inspired Lewis Carroll's Alice's Adventures in Wonderland, spent family holidays in the town, and these days you'll find Alice-themed statues and sculptures dotted around the streets, including the White Rabbit on the West Shore. Following the Alice trail is a brilliant way to keep children busy as you explore, and Mostyn Street makes a good starting point.

The Great Orme, looming over the town, is a full adventure on its own. Look out for the herd of wild Kashmiri goats that roam its slopes, a much-loved local sight. Underground, the Great Orme Copper Mines are Bronze Age workings, thousands of years old, which you can explore on a guided route. It's a fascinating trip back in time and very different from the seaside fun down below.

Back in town, Happy Valley Gardens sit at the foot of the Orme near the pier, with landscaped paths and lovely views, and Venue Cymru on the promenade hosts touring shows, concerts and pantomimes. Mostyn, the contemporary art gallery near Mostyn Street, is a free and calm space to explore if you fancy a culture fix.

For a bigger day out, the medieval walled town of Conwy, with its mighty castle, is just a short hop along the coast. Combine that with a stroll along Llandudno's prom and a bit of shopping in the Victoria Centre, and you've got a proper North Wales day sorted.
